doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Willcox's festivals, Germany trip and Dutch CDs; Whiteman at Bix's grave
summary: Willcox describes Decatur, Sacramento and Davenport festivals, a Wiesbaden trip and two CDs made in Holland; Gallodoro recalls the Whiteman band visiting Bix's grave in 1940.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well you know with me, because in January I go out to Decatur Illinois for a three day festival. People that know Tommy Saunders, he’s the music director of that festival now. And geez, I know enough if I can only think of it. But Sacramento has been a great thing for me and that’s the largest jazz festival in the world now.
I was the Ember last year they made me, and there were a 108,000 people, that gives you an idea. And there were 126 jazz bands there. And I’d just play as a guest, you know.

Yeah. Some of them from New York, and then of course there’s the big Davenport thing where Bix was born, and I don’t know of anyone more qualified now because I’m the last guy I guess that I know of as far as the Goldkette band that played with him now. You know, after all, when you get to be 92, you’ve got to be somewhere near the end of the line. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
But you’re going to Germany too?

Oh, in March, I told you about that, I’m going to go to Wiesbaden, with the Luftsana Airlines are going to fly my daughter and me over, free, and then I’ll go back in Germany. And then this recording, I never dreamed I’d ever make a CD and I made that, I made two now, in Holland though, but the Holland musicians are wonderful. Oh, we could talk a long—
Oh, my goodness. You mentioned Davenport. We played Davenport with the Whiteman band in 1940, early ‘40. And I have photographs of us being at Bix’s home, and the grave, Whiteman and all the guys.
